module_title: Extremist Phase and Swadeshi Movement (1905-1918) - Basic Understanding
introduction: By 1905, a new group emerged within the Congress that was disillusioned with the Moderates' policy of 'prayers and petitions'. They were known as 'Extremists' (Garam Dal). They believed Swaraj (self-rule) had to be achieved through struggle, not requested as a favor. The Partition of Bengal in 1905 turned this phase into a nationwide mass movement.

core_concepts.title: Partition of Bengal (1905)
core_concepts.description: Viceroy Lord Curzon partitioned Bengal in 1905 into East and West Bengal, citing administrative convenience. However, the real motive was to break Hindu-Muslim unity and weaken the rising tide of nationalism.

core_concepts.title: Swadeshi and Boycott Movement
core_concepts.description: In response to the partition, the Swadeshi (use of indigenous goods) and Boycott (rejection of foreign goods) movements were launched. This was India's first major mass movement.

core_concepts.title: Surat Split (1907)
core_concepts.description: Differences over extending the Swadeshi movement outside Bengal and the methods of struggle led to a split in the Congress between the Moderates (Naram Dal) and Extremists (Garam Dal) at the Surat session in 1907.

core_concepts.title: Home Rule League Movement (1916)
core_concepts.description: Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Annie Besant started the Home Rule League movement on the lines of the Irish Home Rule movement to demand self-government for India.

important_entities.name: Lal-Bal-Pal
important_entities.significance: Lala Lajpat Rai (Punjab), Bal Gangadhar Tilak (Maharashtra), and Bipin Chandra Pal (Bengal) were the three main pillars of the extremist ideology.

important_entities.name: Bal Gangadhar Tilak
important_entities.significance: He gave the famous slogan: 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it'.

important_entities.name: Lord Curzon
important_entities.significance: Primarily responsible for the Partition of Bengal (effective from October 16, 1905).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often confuse 'Extremists' with violent revolutionaries. The Extremists' methods were strikes, boycotts, and passive resistance, not bomb and pistol politics.
Tilak and Annie Besant did not form a single joint league. They set up two separate Home Rule Leagues in 1916 (Tilak in April, Besant in September) to avoid friction.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Remember 190'7' for the split between the Moderates and Extremists.

exam_strategy_tips: Dates associated with the Partition of Bengal (Announcement: July 1905, Effective: October 16, 1905) are highly tested.
Questions asking to identify the Extremist leaders (Lal-Bal-Pal + Aurobindo Ghosh) from a given list are very common.
